name: llmc_trimat_forward
goal: Port trimat_forward_harness.cu (llm.c dev/cuda/trimat_forward.cu, fp32 build) to idiomatic SYCL 2020 with zero dpct helpers. Keep every kernel variant k in [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] as its own SYCL kernel, computed on the SYCL device, and keep the program's contract: `build/candidate <input> <output> B T C NH` reads the inputs and writes each variant's outputs in order as raw float32, exactly as the CUDA main does. A hidden reference checks the output (atol 0.0001 + rtol FLT_EPSILON*|ref|, llm.c's own fp32 rule). Success requires compile, verify and a zero-helper scan_helpers of the whole work directory (path '.') on the same sources: migrate's output under migrated/ counts, so replace or empty those files once your own port is done. cuBLAS calls go to oneMath (oneapi::math::blas, #include <oneapi/math.hpp>; the compile flags already link -lonemath), not to oneapi::mkl product APIs.

museport.note: B=2, T=128 (llm.c: B=8, T=1024); C=768, NH=12 as in llm.c. The causal-masked upper triangle is set to 0 in both mains before writing: llm.c's CPU reference writes NaN there and validate_result skips it. cuBLAS runs in fp32 (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH): llm.c's setup_main enables TF32 from Ampere, and with it llm.c's own 1e-4 check of the cuBLAS variant 0 fails (measured: 49484 elements off by up to 2e-4 on an RTX 2000 Ada).
